q-118856.name: Question 1
q-118856.problem: Find the total area of the region bounded by the graph of the curve $y=|x{|}^{3}{e}^{-{x}^{4}}$ and the $x$-axis.
q-118856.worked_solution:
We find the area of the region bounded by the graph of the curve and the $x$-axis by calculating the integral

$$
A={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }|x{|}^{3}{e}^{-{x}^{4}}.
$$

We break up the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }|x{|}^{3}{e}^{-{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}|x{|}^{3}{e}^{-{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }|x{|}^{3}{e}^{-{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x
$$

We start by calculating the first of these integrals:

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}|x{|}^{3}{e}^{-{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x=-{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}{x}^{3}{e}^{-{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x
$$

We calculate the antiderivative using a substitution. Let $u=-{x}^{4}$,  then $\text{d}u=-4{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x.$ Hence, the antiderivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{3}{e}^{-{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{1}{4}\int {e}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}{e}^{u}+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}{e}^{-{x}^{4}}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}|x{|}^{3}{e}^{-{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x & =-{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}{x}^{3}{e}^{-{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{0}{x}^{3}{e}^{-{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{(-\frac{1}{4}{e}^{-{x}^{4}})|}_{a}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }({e}^{0}-{e}^{-{a}^{4}}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(1-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the integrand $|x{|}^{3}{e}^{-{x}^{4}}$ is an **even** function. This means that we can immediately deduce that 

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\infty }|x{|}^{3}{e}^{-{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{4}.
$$

Therefore, since both improper integrals exist, we conclude that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }|x{|}^{3}{e}^{-{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}|x{|}^{3}{e}^{-{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }|x{|}^{3}{e}^{-{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

We find the area of the region bounded by the graph of the curve and the x-axis by calculating the integral A=∫−∞∞|x|3e−x4.

We break up the integral as follows: ∫−∞∞|x|3e−x4dx=∫−∞0|x|3e−x4dx+∫0∞|x|3e−x4dx

We start by calculating the first of these integrals: ∫−∞0|x|3e−x4dx=−∫−∞0x3e−x4dx

We calculate the antiderivative using a substitution. Let u=−x4, then du=−4x3dx. Hence, the antiderivative is ∫x3e−x4dx=−14∫eudu=−14eu+C=−14e−x4+C.

So, we get

∫−∞0|x|3e−x4dx=−∫−∞0x3e−x4dx=−lima→−∞∫a0x3e−x4dx=−lima→−∞(−14e−x4)|a0=14lima→−∞(e0−e−a4)=14(1−0)=14.

Now, notice that the integrand |x|3e−x4 is an even function. This means that we can immediately deduce that

∫0∞|x|3e−x4dx=14.

Therefore, since both improper integrals exist, we conclude that ∫−∞∞|x|3e−x4dx=∫−∞0|x|3e−x4dx+∫0∞|x|3e−x4dx=14+14=12.

q-347615.name: Question 2
q-347615.worked_solution:
We break up the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }\frac{3}{{x}^{2}+25}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{3}{{x}^{2}+25}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{3}{{x}^{2}+25}\,\text{d}x
$$

Evaluating the first of these integrals, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{3}{{x}^{2}+25} & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{0}\frac{3}{{x}^{2}+25}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{25}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{0}\frac{1}{(x/5)^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{25}\cdot 5{lim}_{a\to -\infty }({\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{5})|}_{a}^{0}) \\  & =\frac{3}{5}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }(\operatorname{arctan}⁡0-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{a}{5})) \\  & =\frac{3}{5}(0-(-\frac{\pi }{2})) \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the integrand is an **even** function. This means that we can immediately deduce that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{3}{{x}^{2}+25}\,\text{d}x=\frac{3\pi }{10}.
$$

Therefore, since both improper integrals exist, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }\frac{3}{{x}^{2}+25}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{3}{{x}^{2}+25}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{3}{{x}^{2}+25}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{10}+\frac{3\pi }{10} \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-351545.name: Question 3
q-351545.worked_solution:
We break up the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }\frac{4}{9+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{4}{9+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{4}{9+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Evaluating the first of these integrals, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{4}{9+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{0}\frac{4}{9+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{0}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{(\frac{3}{2})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }({\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{2x}{3})|}_{a}^{0}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡0-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{2a}{3})] \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\cdot [0-(-\frac{\pi }{2})] \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the integrand is an **even** function. This means that we can immediately deduce that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{4}{9+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{\pi }{3}.
$$

Therefore, since both improper integrals exist, we conclude that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }\frac{4}{9+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{4}{9+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{4}{9+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{3} \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the total area $A$ of the region bounded by the graph of the curve $y=5{e}^{-|x|+1}$ and the $x$-axis, as shown above. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
q-351589.worked_solution:
We find the area of the region bounded by the graph of the curve and the $x$-axis by calculating the integral

$$
A={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }5{e}^{-|x|+1}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We break up the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }5{e}^{-|x|+1}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}5{e}^{-|x|+1}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }5{e}^{-|x|+1}\,\text{d}x
$$

Evaluating the first of these integrals, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}5{e}^{-|x|+1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}5{e}^{x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{0}5{e}^{x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5{lim}_{a\to -\infty }({e}^{x+1}{|}_{a}^{0}\,) \\  & =5{lim}_{a\to -\infty }({e}^{0+1}-{e}^{a+1}) \\  & =5(e-0) \\  & =5e.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the integrand $5{e}^{-|x|+1}$ is an **even** function. This means that we can immediately deduce that 

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\infty }5{e}^{-|x|+1}\,\text{d}x=5e.
$$

Therefore, since both improper integrals exist, we conclude that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }5{e}^{-|x|+1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}5{e}^{-|x|+1}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }5{e}^{-|x|+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5e+5e \\  & =10e.\end{aligned}
$$

q-351595.worked_solution:
We find the area of the region bounded by the graph of the curve and the $x$-axis by calculating the integral

$$
A={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }\frac{3}{4+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We break up the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }\frac{3}{4+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{3}{4+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{3}{4+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Evaluating the first of these integrals, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{3}{4+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{0}\frac{3}{4+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{0}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{2}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{lim}_{a\to -\infty }(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2}){|}_{a}^{0}\,) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }(\operatorname{arctan}⁡0-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{a}{2})) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(0-(-\frac{\pi }{2})) \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the integrand is an **even** function. This means that we can immediately deduce that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{3}{4+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{3\pi }{4}.
$$

Therefore, since both improper integrals exist, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }\frac{3}{4+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{3}{4+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{3}{4+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{4}+\frac{3\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
